description: This repository publishes a building-electricity prediction benchmark based on open meter data from 482 non-residential buildings. Its README links raw meter, weather, schedule and metadata inputs, modelling notebooks, results and visualisation notebooks. Users apply scikit-learn regression methods to hourly electricity readings and compare forecast accuracy across building types. The buildings come from the Building Data Genome project; this workflow is a benchmark, not a globally representative stock model. GitHub metadata states MIT licensing for the repository. A limitation is that baseline regression results depend on the selected buildings, temporal split and available covariates; they do not prove which method is best for an unseen building. The workflow can check energy-demand predictors before using them in building-control or power-grid simulations. The paper cited in the README reports the evaluation. No meter table, notebook result or model weights were downloaded.
name: Building meter prediction benchmark workflow
